🔎 What does it actually take to become more visible in AI-generated answers?

We decided to test it on ourselves.

So we put HubSpot’s AEO tool to the test, focusing on one service and tracking our visibility over eight weeks. We began at 8.62%. By the end of the experiment, that had reached 26.63% (currently 32.76%).

One observation caught our attention early: our visibility across AI platforms did not always reflect how well we were performing in traditional search. 🤔 

That prompted us to look more closely at what the AI tools were seeing, follow HubSpot’s AEO recommendations, and make targeted changes based on what we found.💡  

There were two outcomes to the experiment. One changed how often our brand appeared in AI-generated answers. The other gave us a better understanding of the work that still needs to happen beyond what an AEO tool can tell you. 🔍

Have you heard about knowledge debt?

Knowledge debt accumulates when expertise, decisions, processes, customer insights, and operational know-how remain trapped in emails, meetings, documents, and individual employees.

What was previously an efficiency problem has now become an AI problem.

AI systems can only learn from, retrieve, and act upon the knowledge that organisations have made accessible. When critical knowledge remains fragmented or undocumented, AI initiatives often struggle to deliver their full potential.

Many businesses are discovering that successful AI adoption starts long before the technology itself. It begins with creating a structured, connected, and accessible knowledge foundation.

The organisations that solve their knowledge debt problem today may have a significant advantage in the AI-native economy tomorrow.

How much of your organisation's most valuable knowledge is actually available for AI to use?

Mid-sized companies face the toughest squeeze, caught between AI-native challengers and bundled incumbents.
